Ardian Semiconductor's €1 billion includes close to €700 million of fund commitments, with the rest in co-investments [1].

MENA investors provided 41% of the capital and French investors 24%; new investors made up 58% of commitments [1].

The platform has invested in four companies: VSORA, centrotherm, Synergie CAD and Ion Beam Services [1].

Ardian has raised €1 billion for Ardian Semiconductor, which the Paris-based investment firm describes as one of the first private equity strategies dedicated to the semiconductor value chain [1]. The total is about $1.12 billion, Reuters reported [2]. Close to €700 million is fund commitments, and the rest comes from co-investments; Ardian did not say how much co-investment capital it raised [1].

Investors from the Middle East and North Africa supplied 41% of the capital and French investors 24% [1]. The backers include government agencies, sovereign wealth funds, semiconductor companies, insurers and private wealth clients, though Ardian named none of them. New investors to Ardian accounted for 58% of commitments [1].

The platform was formed through an exclusive partnership with Silian Partners, a group of former senior semiconductor executives who work with Ardian as one team. It invests mainly in European chip companies and also has a pipeline in North America and Asia [1]. Ardian is targeting specialty chips such as power, analog and photonics, plus IP, equipment, materials and consumables, and pointed to Semiconductor Industry Association data showing global chip sales passed $1 trillion in the first eight months of 2026 [1].

Its four holdings are VSORA, a French fabless designer of AI inference accelerators for data centers; centrotherm, a German maker of thermal processing equipment used for silicon carbide power devices; Synergie CAD, a French test-interface company; and Ion Beam Services, a French ion implantation equipment and services firm [1].

"Semiconductors are a highly specialized market where expertise is critical to identifying the strongest opportunities," said Lise Fauconnier, co-head of Ardian Semiconductor [1]. The fund has also been selected under France's Tibi initiative and is a member of the Ministry of Armed Forces' Defense Investor Club [1].
